segments.narration: Seventy uncut diamonds vanished from a locked vault with zero witnesses. This happened in London's Hatton Garden back in 1913, inside the most heavily guarded merchant district in Europe.
The courier delivered a heavy lead-sealed package directly to the chief merchant's desk. The ledger was signed, the receipt was stamped, and the box was slid onto the top shelf of the safe.

Yet when the safe was opened twenty minutes later, investigators found no scratches on the heavy steel lock and no tunnels beneath the floorboards. How do you steal a fortune when the door was never even picked?

The twist is that the theft happened long before the box ever touched the vault. Police tracked a corrupt courier who had systematically swapped the parcel out for lead weights weeks earlier during transit.
The missing gems were already melted down in a back-alley jeweler's shop three days before the alarm was raised. The perfect crime wasn't magic—it was just paperwork.
